_comment: Chunk-level retrieval probes for the pdf/ corpus (66 pages, 6 subjects).
Gold is an answer SPAN, not a chunk id, because chunk boundaries differ between
configurations — a retrieved chunk counts as correct when it contains the span.
Every span was verified to appear in the BODY of exactly one page, so the gold page
is unambiguous. Spans found only in a page's trailing 關鍵字 line are rejected: that
line can land in a different chunk from the content it describes.
Probes concentrate on the dense regions where pages genuinely compete — 18 biology
pages on plant hormones, 10 history pages on modern China, 21 C++ pages — because
that is where chunking can actually change the ranking.
page: gold page id, matching the '<file>#pNN' units the experiment ingests
2026-08-31 correction: cs-pointer and cs-structured-binding originally used the
spans 記憶體位址 and 結構化綁定. Manual correction against the manuscript showed
neither phrase is written on the page — Gemini added them in B1. Verified: 記憶體位址
appears in B1's text only, 結構化綁定 in B1 and B4 only, both absent from B0. Those
probes therefore scored extraction invention, not retrieval, and penalised whichever
config was more faithful. Spans replaced with terms present in all three corpora and
unique to one page each.
2026-09-07 correction: six probes had their gold span written verbatim in their own
question (bio-triple 三重反應, bio-aril 假種皮, bio-hypogeal 子葉不出土型,
bio-stone-cell 石細胞, phys-areal 面積速率, phys-atomic 原子力). Those measured literal
string overlap rather than retrieval, and pushed every configuration toward the
ceiling together. Questions rewritten from the manuscript so the span no longer
appears in them; spans and gold pages unchanged, so n stays 29. bio-aril was also
retyped fact -> its rewritten form asks for a single fact, not a hierarchy relation.
